defs_parts: Eight labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Editor or docs: the term comes from the editor itself or its official documentation.
Outside source: the term comes from a source outside the course text.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: An Animation is data, and an AnimationPlayer is the node that plays it.
A track binds one property, and its keys are the points it passes through.
A method track calls a function, and it never fires while you scrub.
A tween reads its end value from gameplay, and can be killed halfway.
Inverse kinematics sets the target and solves the angles, and a pole picks the bend.
Read the pose in skeleton updated, and pin the time step before you test.
bookends.command: Give me short cases from making a game in Godot, one at a time, each showing an animation idea at work. Draw on AnimationPlayer, track, key, playhead, method track, update mode, loop seam, Tween, inverse kinematics and pole target. I answer with the exact term and say why its look-alike does not fit. Wait for my answer before you reveal yours.
checks: Check: every case comes from making a game, and waits for your answer.
Check: you named the exact term and ruled out its look-alike.
